justifications.durability: both repair paths carry mutation controls: restoring the original claim query makes the concurrent-claim test fail with eight claims for four files, and restoring the scored-status filter in _refresh_ingestion_claims makes the mixed-status test fail (I reproduced the latter: EXIT=1, 'Code ingestion claim changed while its holder was active'), while the fix passes. Failure marking is now guarded by token and scored status, so a lost-claim worker cannot downgrade a file. Residual risk is that both live probes are bounded and neither reproduces a real long ingestion batch, and the shared claim_batch keeps the unfixed two-step pattern.
justifications.evidence: the head gate (106 passed at e5daecb1) is reproduced by an independent head arm, and a comparable base arm at f90e2e05 (102 passed) closes the added-failure question at zero; the terminal-status defect is independently reproduced by my own mutation and refuted at the fix. Gaps are that the reviewed manifest carries no baseline_suite, and that four gate-log headers name a revision the measured tree was not at.
justifications.fit: the facility write-lock is a recognisable Neo4j serialization idiom, the renewal helper and guards reuse the existing claim_token and claim-timeout constant, tests are named by mechanism, commits carry conventional subjects with bodies, and no plan, sprint, ticket or author identifier appears in the code, tests, fragment or messages (checked).
justifications.goal_fidelity: the cause is named from the retry receipt and corroborated by the concurrent-claim test; claim selection is serialized on the facility so two workers take each file once; a working batch renews its own token-checked claim; and the resumed commits repair the terminal-status renewal defect the first head carried, with the mixed-status and lost-token tests now green at the committed head.
justifications.reuse: the change serializes through the existing Facility node and reuses claim_token, GraphClient, DEFAULT_CLAIM_TIMEOUT_SECONDS and asyncio.to_thread; it introduces no parallel lock service. It does, however, re-implement the claim/renewal shape locally in code/workers.py rather than generalising the shared helpers in discovery/base/claims.py, where claim_batch retains the same two-step pattern.
justifications.scope_discipline: the reviewed diff stays exactly inside the declared write scope across all six commits and adds no unrelated edits; the earlier partial-run finding (a dirty worktree beyond head 16cded4a recorded 'complete') is resolved by the later commits and the worktree is clean at e5daecb1.
